incident-bot: :rotating_light: p95 latency SLO breach detected for /v1/generate in us-west-1. p95=1150ms (SLO 500ms) across gateway-101. Triggered routing policy evaluation.

morgan: paging oncall-eng @sana @omar — can you triage? impact looks multi-customer (hosted API).

sana: on it. just landed oncall. grabbing logs now. initial glance: repeated routing decisions in the last 6m.

lee: past 12 lines from routing-decider:
```
2026-03-15T10:05:02Z route_eval userseg=prod p95=620 -> reroute target=eu-central variant=gptx-v2:quant cooldown=30s
2026-03-15T10:05:35Z route_eval userseg=prod p95=440 -> reroute target=us-west-1 variant=gptx-v2:fast cooldown=30s
2026-03-15T10:06:11Z route_eval userseg=prod p95=670 -> reroute target=eu-central variant=gptx-v2:quant cooldown=30s
2026-03-15T10:06:38Z route_eval userseg=prod p95=380 -> reroute target=us-west-1 variant=gptx-v2:fast cooldown=30s
```
This matches the spike pattern. looks like switching every ~30s.

omar: that pattern screams "too-aggressive threshold + short cooldown". Also noticed routing policy references exact model alias `gptx-v2:quant` for fallback — that variant is quantized but has a cold-warmup penalty on our runtime for seq len>512. unhappy path.

morgan: so two vectors: policy sensitivity causing flip-flopping, and the fallback variant is actually slower under current load. any quick wins?

sana: immediate mitigation proposal: 1) disable autoswitching on the policy for the affected customer bucket 2) increase cooldown to 10m 3) change fallback variant to `gptx-v2:fast` (pin) 4) open a status page note.

omar: +1. I'll take (1) and (2) now. executing change in control-plane.

devbot: deploy-bot: control-plane change requested by omar — patch id cp-9821 — applying policy update ...

devbot: deploy-bot: patch cp-9821 applied to policy routing/prod/high-sensitivity (disabled autoswitch, cooldown=600s) — roll forward OK.

lee: after the patch: routing-decider logs show no further flip in last 3m. p95 back down to ~480ms.

morgan: good. omar can you also pin the model alias for impacted route? we want to avoid fallback to quantized variant until we dig deeper.

omar: doing pin now — updating policy to target `gptx-v2:fast` for primary+fallback. patch cp-9822.

devbot: deploy-bot: patch cp-9822 applied — model target pinned.

cs-rep-jen: drafting incident blurb for affected customers: short note, ETA for RCA, mitigation steps taken, ask if they saw degraded latency or errors. I'll post to customers under status page. LMK if wording edit.

sana: quick note for the postmortem: root cause surfaces as miscalibrated routing rule (threshold too low) + accidental selection of a slower variant as fallback. also need better circuit-breaker to avoid rapid cross-region failover.

morgan: agreed. action items assigned:
- oma r: confirm telemetry of model-variant latency and warmup curves (omar)
- infra: add safety cooldown default and max-switch-per-window (lee)
- eng-ml: add variant performance metadata to model catalog so policy can prefer warm variants (omar + sana)
- product: review default routing sensitivity (morgan + product)

support-bot: statuspage: "Investigating - Increased latency observed for text generation API in us-west-1. Temporary mitigation applied; autoswitching disabled for impacted routes. Customer performance should be improving. Follow-up update will be posted."

morgan: closing oncall handoff — we'll keep this as P1 for follow-up RCA. tagging postmortem owners: sana (lead), lee (infra), omar (model perf).

omar: final note — need a small change to routing-decider: prefer fallback variants with verified tail-latency <= primary * 1.1, otherwise choose a lower-cost-but-faster variant. I'll include a test harness PR.

sana: thanks all. monitoring for 30m and then I'll mark as mitigated in the incident tracker. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident update: mitigated (controls changed) at 2026-03-15T10:14:50Z. Incident still open for RCA and postmortem.
